title: Bouillabaisse
subtitle: Provençal saffron fish stew with rouille
excerpt: The great fish stew of Marseille: a fragrant broth of saffron, fennel, tomatoes, and garlic in which mixed firm-fleshed fish and shellfish are cooked briefly and served with slices of toasted bread and rouille, the garlic and saffron mayonnaise.

recipe.sourceNotes: Bouillabaisse is the defining dish of Marseille and one of the most famous fish preparations in the world. The word derives from two Provençal verbs meaning to boil and to lower: the technique of bringing the broth to a high boil, then reducing the heat to cook the fish, which prevents the fat from the fish emulsifying with the broth. The traditional Marseille version specifies that at least four of a list of local Mediterranean fish varieties must be used, including scorpion fish (rascasse), which gives the broth its characteristic flavour. Outside the Mediterranean, a combination of firm white fish and shellfish approximates the character of the dish. The rouille (which means rust in Provençal) is the essential accompaniment: a thick mayonnaise of garlic, saffron, egg yolk, and olive oil, spread onto toasted bread (croûtons) and floated in the broth or served alongside.

content.text: Build the broth first and cook the fish in it at the very end: fish takes only minutes and must not be overcooked. Add the firmest fish first, then the shellfish, then the most delicate fillets. The broth can be made a day ahead; add the fish only when ready to serve.

items.preparation: cut into 5 cm chunks; or monkfish, sea bass, or a mixture of firm white fish
trimmed and thinly sliced; fronds reserved to finish
zest only; a strip of peel added to the broth

content.text: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and fennel for 10 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, chilli flakes, and tomato purée and cook for 2 minutes. Add the wine and let it bubble for 1 minute. Add the tinned tomatoes, fish stock, saffron with its soaking water, orange peel, and bay leaves. Simmer for 25 minutes.

Season the broth with salt. Bring to a rolling boil. Add the prawns and cook for 2 minutes. Add the fish chunks and cook for 3 minutes. Add the mussels and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until all the mussels have opened; discard any that remain closed. Remove the bay leaves and orange peel.

Serve in wide bowls with the fennel fronds scattered over. Accompany with toasted slices of bread spread with rouille (blend together 2 garlic cloves, a pinch of saffron, 1 egg yolk, 150 ml olive oil, salt, and a little lemon juice to make a thick garlic mayonnaise).
